title: The Locked Gate
subtitle: Four hundred students have the wrong hall tickets on exam morning
coldOpen: 08:15. A printing error puts wrong centres on 400 tickets.
08:40. Students are locked out; the exam starts at nine.
Parents want the exam cancelled for everyone.

briefing.grievance: Four hundred students were sent to the wrong centre by a printing error and are locked out of a career exam. They want in, today, with the same paper as everyone else.
knownFacts: The error affects 400 of 12,000 candidates; the board confirms it is its own mistake.
The exam has started on time at all other centres.
A second sitting is possible this afternoon with the reserve paper.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the reserve paper has already leaked.
A message says the board will cancel the whole exam at noon.
briefing.responsibility: You run the board’s crisis desk and the campus police liaison. Fairness to 400 and fairness to 11,600 are both your job.
briefing.objective: Get the 400 a fair sitting today, keep the other 11,600 results valid, and keep the campus calm.

decisions.title: Locked out at nine
decisions.situation: Four hundred students are at the gate with the wrong tickets. The exam inside has started. Parents are shouting “cancel it for everyone”.

options.title: Announce a 2 pm sitting on the reserve paper
options.preview: The 400 sit at 2 pm, same centre, sealed reserve paper.
options.authority: Duty of candour: say what is known and what is not
options.consequence: The gate crowd has a time. The inside exam continues.

options.title: Meet the council and the parents at the gate
options.preview: You admit the error and ask for an hour to confirm the reserve paper.
options.authority: Duty to hear grievances; Article 19(1)(a) free expression
options.consequence: The admission lands. The shouting becomes a queue of questions.

options.title: Cancel the exam for all 12,000
options.preview: The exam is stopped at every centre; a new date later.
options.authority: Fairness: a remedy must not harm those who were not wronged
options.consequence: Eleven thousand six hundred students lose a valid paper to fix 400 tickets.

delayed.message: Students who finished the exam march to the board demanding their papers be counted.

options.title: Wait for the board chairman
options.preview: No decision until he calls back.
options.consequence: The exam inside is half over and the 400 are still at the gate.

decisions.title: Is the reserve paper safe?
decisions.situation: A post says the reserve paper leaked. The custody log says the seal is intact. Parents will not accept an afternoon sitting on a leaked paper.

options.title: Verify the seal with the council watching
options.preview: Two council members and a parent inspect the sealed set and sign the log.
options.authority: Due process: establish the facts before acting on them
options.consequence: The seal is intact, witnessed. The post is answered with a signature.

options.title: Escort the reserve paper to the centre now
options.preview: The sealed set travels under escort and is opened only in the hall.
options.authority: Duty to keep essential services running
options.consequence: The paper is in the building before the rumour is.

options.title: Announce the reserve paper is compromised
options.preview: The board adopts the post and withdraws the afternoon sitting.
options.authority: Due process: a public charge needs verified evidence
options.consequence: A sealed, untouched paper is declared leaked because of a photo of last year’s questions.

options.title: Ignore the post
options.preview: Parents keep forwarding it; some pull their children out of the sitting.
options.consequence: Doubt spreads where facts could have.

simple.title: Is the spare paper safe?

o-d012-2-accuse.title: Say the spare paper leaked

o-d012-2-wait.title: Ignore the post
o-d012-2-wait.preview: Parents keep sharing it. Some pull their children out.

decisions.title: The road to the board office
decisions.situation: Parents have blocked the road to the board office demanding the chairman. The afternoon sitting is in three hours. The campus is tense.

options.title: Bring the chairman to the parents
options.preview: He speaks at the block; marshals from the council keep one lane open.
options.authority: Article 19(1)(b): peaceful assembly, policed in proportion
options.consequence: The chairman answers in person. The block becomes a meeting.

options.title: Move the few blocking the exam convoy
options.preview: Officers clear only the convoy’s path, with the council watching.
options.authority: Proportionality: act against the few causing harm, not the many
options.consequence: The paper gets through. The parents stay.

options.title: Detain the parents leading the block
options.preview: Twelve parents are taken to the station for obstruction.
options.authority: Articles 21 and 22: liberty and safeguards on arrest
options.consequence: Parents of locked-out students are in cells on exam day.

delayed.message: The crackdown hardens people who had stayed out of it. More arrive, angrier.

options.title: Let the block stand

decisions.title: Two o’clock

rightsMoments.question: A board error locked 400 students out of an exam. What does a fair remedy look like?

options.text: Restore the 400 to an equal position, with a sitting of equal weight, without harming the 11,600 who sat properly.
options.feedback: Correct. Equality means repairing the harm to those affected without creating a new harm to others.

options.text: Cancel everyone’s exam so that all are treated identically.
options.feedback: Identical treatment is not equal treatment when it punishes those who were not wronged.

options.text: Give the 400 bonus marks on next year’s exam.
options.feedback: A deferred, unequal remedy does not restore the right that was lost today.

rightsMoments.principle: Article 14 requires equal treatment, which includes an effective, proportionate remedy for those a state error has harmed, without arbitrarily harming others.
rightsMoments.why: An afternoon sitting of equal weight restored the 400 without voiding 11,600 valid papers.

simple.question: A board mistake locked 400 students out of an exam. What is a fair fix?

options.a: Give the 400 an equal exam today, without hurting the other 11,600.
options.b: Cancel everyone’s exam so all are treated the same.
options.c: Give the 400 extra marks next year.

feedback.a: Yes! Fix the harm without creating a new one.
feedback.c: A late, unequal fix does not give back what was lost today.

simple.principle: Everyone is treated fairly. Fix a mistake for those hurt by it, without hurting others.
simple.why: An afternoon exam of equal weight fixed things for the 400 without cancelling 11,600 valid papers.

events.message: A speaker tells the parents the afternoon sitting is a trick and the paper is “already sold”.
events.simple: A speaker tells parents the afternoon exam is a trick.

events.message: The morning sitting ends; 1,180 students walk out past the 400 still at the gate.
events.simple: The morning exam ends. The 400 are still at the gate.

resolved.text: The 400 got a same-day sitting on the sealed reserve paper.
The reserve paper’s seal was verified in front of students and parents.
resolved.simple: The spare paper was checked in front of witnesses.

resolved.text: Both sittings were declared equal in writing.

unresolved.text: Twelve thousand students lost a valid exam to fix a printing error.
unresolved.simple: Twelve thousand students lost their exam.

unresolved.text: The leak rumour was never answered; the afternoon paper carries a shadow.
unresolved.simple: The leak rumour was never answered.

unresolved.text: Nobody said both sittings count the same.
unresolved.simple: Nobody said both exams count the same.

rightsProtected.text: Parents kept their protest while the paper reached the hall.
rightsProtected.simple: Parents kept their protest. The paper reached the hall.

rightsProtected.text: The board admitted its own error in public.
rightsProtected.simple: The board admitted its mistake in public.

rightsHarmed.text: Parents were detained on their children’s exam day.
rightsHarmed.simple: Parents were detained on exam day.

rightsHarmed.text: Students who did nothing wrong lost their results.

improvements.text: Announce the remedy before the crowd announces a demand.
improvements.simple: Announce the fix before the crowd demands one.

improvements.text: Let witnesses see the seal; a photo of last year’s paper cannot survive that.
A remedy that voids 11,600 valid papers is not fairness; it is a second error.
improvements.simple: Cancelling everyone is a second mistake.

closing.good: Four hundred sat at two o’clock on a paper everyone had seen sealed, and the morning’s papers were never in doubt.
closing.mixed: The 400 got their sitting, but late and under a cloud, and the board still has not said the two papers are equal.
closing.poor: A printing error became a cancelled exam, and twelve thousand students are now the grievance.

briefing.grievance: Four hundred students went to the wrong centre because of a printing error. They are locked out of a big exam.
knownFacts: The error hit 400 of 12,000 students. The board admits it.
The exam started on time elsewhere.
A second sitting is possible this afternoon.
unverifiedClaims: A post says the spare paper already leaked.
A message says the whole exam will be cancelled at noon.
